correctness.rationale: An independent uniform argument uses dephasing to put 1s in the first row and column and four unit complex entries A,B,C,D in the lower block. Singularity is (A-1)(D-1)=(B-1)(C-1). If both sides are nonzero, conjugation gives AD=BC, and expansion gives A+D=B+C. The unordered pairs then agree, forcing duplicate rows or columns. If both sides vanish, one entry from each product equals 1; those entries share a row or column, which duplicates the first row or column. In the original Fourier minor two rows are proportional iff N divides their index difference times every column difference. At N=3p a nonzero such row difference divisible by p forces all column indices to agree mod 3, and one divisible by 3 forces them to agree mod p; a unit cannot yield proportionality. Transpose for columns. This recovers all four singularity clauses, including p=5. Rank one requires all pair products divisible by both primes, giving exactly the two cross-pure cases. There are p triples pure mod p, 3*binom(p,3) pure mod 3, and K-p^3 and K-27*binom(p,3) triples with collisions mod 3 and p respectively (K=binom(3p,3)). In the four singular events the only pairwise overlaps are the two cross-pure rank-one blocks. Inclusion-exclusion gives the stated polynomials. Independent exact Phi_N reduction checks all 207025 pairs at p=5 and 18000 seeded pairs each at p=7,13,19 without mismatch.
